Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates pneumomediastinum with lucent streaks of air extending throughout the mediastinum and into the neck, which is characteristic of alveolar rupture (Macklin effect) often precipitated by vomiting or increased intrathoracic pressure during an alcoholic binge. Esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome) typically presents with more severe systemic toxicity and pleural effusion, whereas this pattern of extensive anterior mediastinal and cervical emphysema in a young male post-binge strongly favors a benign spontaneous etiology from alveolar overdistension.
